'''''Triglochin striata''''' is a species of [[flowering plant]] in the family ''[[Juncaginaceae]]''.<ref name=POWO>{{cite web |url= https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:603563-1 |title= Triglochin striata Ruiz & Pav. |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=n.d. |website=Plants of the World Online |publisher=The Trustees of the Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew |access-date=January 18, 2025}}</ref><ref name=COL>{{cite web |url= https://www.catalogueoflife.org/data/taxon/58QMX |title= Triglochin striata Ruiz & Pav. |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=n.d. |website=Catalogue of Life |publisher=Species 2000 |access-date=January 18, 2025}}</ref> It is native to [[New Zealand]], South America, America, Africa, Australia and Southern Portugal.<ref>[http://www.alocasia.com.au/qld_saltmarsh_plants/herbarium/grasses-rushes-and-sedge-plants/streaked-arrow-grass Online Field Guide to Common Saltmarsh Plants of Queensland] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091017115303/http://www.alocasia.com.au/qld_saltmarsh_plants/herbarium/grasses-rushes-and-sedge-plants/streaked-arrow-grass |date=2009-10-17 }}</ref><ref>{{GRIN | accessdate = 19 January 2018}}</ref><ref name="NZPCN">{{Cite web|url=http://www.nzpcn.org.nz/flora_details.aspx?ID=2277|title=Triglochin striata {{!}} New Zealand Plant Conservation Network|website=www.nzpcn.org.nz|access-date=2020-01-04}}</ref> 

It is a [[Perennial plant|perennial]] with parallel lines on its narrow linear leaves, which gives rise to its common name '''streaked arrow grass'''. Other common names include '''three-rib arrowgrass'''<ref>{{PLANTS|id=TRST16|taxon=Triglochin striata|accessdate=15 December 2015}}</ref> and '''three-ribbed arrow-grass'''.

==Habitat==
''Triglochin striata''{{'}}s habitat is mainly coastal in damp muddy ground, [[salt marsh]], [[Estuary|estuaries]], and damp [[Seepage spring|seepages]] on coastal cliffs, boulder beaches and within damp coastal turf. It is also found inland around lake margins (in marginal turf communities) and in other suitable damp places, and sometimes even in tall forest.<ref name="NZPCN"/>
